ActivityDayRow.description: One local day's volume. Empty days are present, never trimmed.
ActivityDayRow.title: ActivityDayRow

ActivityHourRow.description:
One hour of the LOCAL day, summed across the window.

Asia/Tashkent, never UTC: "customers cannot get through at lunchtime" is
visible at 12:00 and becomes a meaningless 07:00 in UTC. Identical shape to
the daily row, because one chart draws both cuts.
ActivityHourRow.title: ActivityHourRow

ActivityResponse.description: The whole report: window, chart series, per-agent rows and the total.

callback_median_minutes.description: Company-wide median minutes to contact. Computed over calls, never as an average of the agents' medians — a median of medians ignores volume.

callback_window_hours.description: A later call counts as a callback only inside this many hours.

date_to.description: Inclusive: the last day the window covers.

total.description: The company row. Its customer counts are computed separately, not summed: one customer who called two employees is one person.

ActivityResponse.title: ActivityResponse

AgentActivityRow.description: One employee over the window. The company total uses the same shape.

callback_median_minutes.description: How long this employee keeps a customer waiting (median minutes). A different question from the rate: 100 % returned three hours later is a good rate and a bad service.

callback_rate.description: Reached as a percent of unreached customers, per CUSTOMER.

clients_unreached.description: THE HEADLINE: lost business, counted in people rather than calls.

inbound_total.description: Calls customers made to the employee.

missed.description: INCOMING and not answered — the company's responsibility, and the point of this report. `rejected` counts here with `missed`: the phone rang and there was no conversation.

missed_addressable.description: Missed events carrying a usable number. `missed_open` divides by this, because a number nobody has cannot be called back.

missed_clients.description: Distinct customers who could not get through; repeat attempts count once. Measured: 1.8 attempts per customer on average.

missed_rate.description: Missed as a percent of incoming. Null when there were none.

outbound_no_answer.description: The customer did not pick up. NOT a missed call and never added to one: measured over 7 days, 983 incoming unanswered against 1047 outgoing, so combining them doubles the figure and blames the employee for it.

outbound_total.description: Calls the employee made to customers.

AgentActivityRow.title: AgentActivityRow

AgentBreakdownOut.description: One employee's slice of the report.

agent_id.description: Null — sales whose branch is linked to nobody.

new.description: Suspicious and not yet decided — the work queue.

AgentBreakdownOut.title: AgentBreakdownOut

AgentRankRowOut.description: One agent's standing over the window.

rank_delta.description: Places gained against the previous period; positive means moved up. Null for an agent who scored nothing in that period.

AgentRankRowOut.title: AgentRankRowOut

total.description: Agents with at least one scored call.

AlertKind.description:
Every cause that can raise an alert (SPEC §10.3).

SPEC §3.1 says "24 values"; §10.3's table groups the three
``permission_lost_*`` causes on one line and pairs
``retention_job_failed``/``backup_failed`` on another. Expanded, release 1's
closed set was the first 27 below — the count in §3.1 is a count of table
rows.

The last two arrive with the analysis module (SPEC-ANALYTICS §2.1, §5,
migration 011) and each exists because the nearest existing value would
point an admin at the wrong subsystem: a stalled AI pipeline raising
``retention_job_failed`` sends somebody to look at deletion, and a monthly
cap stopping the queue is not a failure at all — it is the safety rail
working, and it needs a name that says so.
AlertKind.title: AlertKind

AlertResponse.description: One open or acknowledged alert, as the inbox renders it.

body_uz.description: What to do about it. Derived from `kind`, not stored.

installation_status.description: Status of the installation this alert is about. New alerts are not raised against a superseded phone and its open ones are closed when it is replaced — this is here so a page can also tell at a glance, without a second query, for alerts raised before that rule existed.

occurrence_count.description: Repeats bump this rather than inserting a row: a phone reporting every two minutes must not produce 720 rows a day.

title_uz.description: What happened, in Uzbek. Derived from `kind`, not stored.

AlertResponse.title: AlertResponse

AnalysisCallHeader.description:
Which conversation this is (§7.4).

Carried in the analysis response on purpose: the detail page must say
*whose call, when, with whom and how long* without sending the reader to
the calls section to find out. The analysis section is a section of its own
(§7), so a link there is a navigation away from the page, not a tooltip.

``agent_name`` is resolved server-side for the same reason
``CallResponse`` resolves it — a name lookup per row in the browser is the
N+1 problem with a different owner.

call_type.description: Why a call was or was not scored: only `external` is scored, and `unknown` means the line directory cannot tell yet (§2.6).

remote_number.description: As the device saw it. NULL when the caller withheld it.

started_at.description: When the conversation happened. The list sorts on this (§7.3).

AnalysisCallHeader.title: AnalysisCallHeader

AnalysisFailure.description:
Why a call stopped. Closed, and ``NOT NULL`` whenever the stage is
``skipped`` or ``failed`` (a CHECK on ``call_analysis_state``).

``stage`` says whether the row is terminal; this says why. The three groups
below are not decoration — only the transient ones are re-queued by
``analysis_retry_transient``, and getting that membership wrong is how 885
rate-limited calls stayed permanently failed in BonviZvonki after the quota
they were waiting on had reset.
AnalysisFailure.title: AnalysisFailure

AnalysisFailureRow.description: One recent failure, with enough to act on it (§7.5).

stage.description: Which half was running: transcribe | score.

AnalysisFailureRow.title: AnalysisFailureRow

AnalysisListItem.description:
One row of the scored-call list (§7.3).

The columns §7.3 names and nothing more. No transcript text: a list of
fifty conversations is not a place to ship fifty transcripts, and the
detail page is one click away.

overall_score.description: NULL until the call is scored — a queued row still has a place in the list.

red_flag_types.description: Sorted and de-duplicated, for the chips. The quotes stay on the detail page: a customer's words do not belong in a list payload.

AnalysisListItem.title: AnalysisListItem

AnalysisListResponse.description: A cursor page of analysed calls, newest conversation first (§7.3).

total.description: Counted only when asked, exactly as /calls does it.

AnalysisListResponse.title: AnalysisListResponse

AnalysisMonthResponse.description:
This Tashkent calendar month's spend against the caps (§4.5, §11.1).

Tashkent and not UTC because the person reading the bill lives there: a
month turning over at 05:00 local would put the first five hours of every
month into the previous one's cap.

audio_minutes.description: Measured ASR input — the billing unit.

calls.description: State rows that reached `completed` this month.

cap_calls.description: The cap that actually protects the account until a price is entered, because an unpriced month can never reach the money one.

date_from.description: First day of the current Asia/Tashkent month. Named like every other window in this API; §6.2 sketched it as `from`, which is not a Python identifier.

priced.description: Whether any vendor price has been entered. **False is what stops the panel rendering $0.00 and implying the feature is free** — a cost of zero because nobody typed a price is not a free feature.

AnalysisMonthResponse.title: AnalysisMonthResponse

AnalysisStage.description:
Where one call stands in the analysis pipeline (SPEC-ANALYTICS §2.4).

The state row *is* the status: there is no ``calls.status`` column and
nothing on ``calls`` is written by the analysis module.

BonviZvonki's ``locked`` is deliberately absent. Locking is the claim query
(``FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED``) plus the worker's advisory lock, and neither
survives a crash — a persisted ``locked`` would, leaving a row that no
dispatch picks up and no operator can explain.
AnalysisStage.title: AnalysisStage

AnalysisStageCounts.description:
Calls per stage. One field per ``AnalysisStage`` member, always present.

A fixed object rather than a map, so a stage with nothing in it is a
visible zero instead of an absent key the panel has to default. The six
fields are pinned against the enum by a test.

skipped.description: **Not a failure** and the panel must not paint it as one (§2.4).

AnalysisStageCounts.title: AnalysisStageCounts

AnalysisStateResponse.description:
``call_analysis_state`` as the panel reads it (§6.2).

Also the whole answer to ``POST /analysis/calls/{id}``: queueing returns
the state and nothing else, so a first press and a re-press are
indistinguishable (§5's shape, applied to a panel write).

asr_calls.description: Requests that reached a provider, i.e. that cost money.

cost_micro_usd.description: Measured units x the admin-entered price. 0 also means **not priced** — see `AnalysisMonthResponse.priced` (§11.1).

failure_code.description: Why the call stopped. Present exactly when the stage is `failed` or `skipped` — a database CHECK, not a habit. The Uzbek headline is keyed off this in the panel's uz.json.

failure_detail.description: The provider's own message, redacted. Technical English beside the code, never the sentence a user reads.

failure_stage.description: `transcribe` or `score` — which half spent money before stopping.

AnalysisStateResponse.title: AnalysisStateResponse

AnalysisStatusResponse.description:
The operational view: what is waiting, what broke, what it cost (§7.5).

This is where an admin answers "why has nothing been scored since
Tuesday". It exists in phase 1 because without it that question has no
answer short of opening the database.

cooldowns.description: Only the roles currently sitting out; empty is the normal state.

not_analysable.description: Skips by reason, so '412 calls are waiting on the line directory' is visible rather than silent (§2.6).

recent_failures.description: Newest first, capped at 20 server-side. Not a paged list (§6.2).

waiting_retry.description: Failed on a transient code and inside the nightly retry's reach, so it will be tried again by itself. Separate from `stages.failed` on purpose: one of them needs a person and the other does not.

AnalysisStatusResponse.title: AnalysisStatusResponse

avg_duration_sec.description: Mean call length over the scored calls, rounded half up.

calls.description: **Scored** calls — the join to call_scores is an inner one. A call the pipeline skipped or has not reached is not in it; call_types below is what accounts for the difference.

calls_total.description: Every call in the window, scored or not.

compared_with.description: The window every delta_percent above is measured against.

red_flags.description: Scored calls carrying at least one red flag, not flags found.

filled.description: True when every period in the window is present, empty ones included. False past the 550-period ceiling, where only periods with data are returned — the panel then draws what it was given rather than pretending the axis is complete.

AnalyticsWindow.description:
The window a report was computed over, echoed back.

On every response, because five of the six are opened without naming a
window at all — the caller asked for "the last 30 days" and the page has to
be able to say which days those were.
AnalyticsWindow.title: AnalyticsWindow

AppVariant.description:
The ``targetSdk`` product flavour (D-06).

Reported on every heartbeat, stored on every call, so capture rate is
measurable per variant and not only per handset model.
AppVariant.title: AppVariant

signing_sha256_configured.description: Whether a signing fingerprint is configured. False means uploads are accepted without the key check — see docs/APK-SIGNING.md.

AppVersionResponse.description: One build in the distribution record.

created_by_name.description: Who uploaded it, resolved server-side. The id alone would make every page re-solve it through `GET /users`, which a manager cannot read — so a manager would see a bare uuid.

published_at.description: NULL means uploaded but not published — reaches nobody.

AppVersionResponse.title: AppVersionResponse

AssignBranchRequest.description:
One change to the map. BOTH fields are optional.

They answer SEPARATE questions and do not substitute for one another —
"who is responsible" and "is this branch checked at all" — so a field that
is not sent is NOT touched. `agent_id: null` is a full value ("unlink"),
which is different from "not sent".

excluded.description: `true` — take the branch out of sales control (its sales move to the out-of-scope section and are NOT deleted); `false` — put it back (the whole history returns with no re-import); omitted — leave it alone.

AssignBranchRequest.title: AssignBranchRequest

AssignmentListResponse.description: Full history for a number — this is the timeline the agent page renders.
AssignmentListResponse.title: AssignmentListResponse

AttestRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/installations/{id}/attest`` (T142).

Attestation is deliberately weaker evidence than a proven binding, and the
reason is mandatory: an unexplained attestation is indistinguishable from a
mistake six months later.
AttestRequest.title: AttestRequest

AudioMissingReason.description:
Why a call has no audio. Closed, ``NOT NULL`` whenever audio is absent (N5).

UC-14 names six; SPEC §3.9 justifies the other four one by one. The gap
report's denominator excludes ``pending_upload`` and ``not_expected``,
which is what keeps "% of answered calls with audio" honest.
AudioMissingReason.title: AudioMissingReason

AuditAction.description:
Every auditable action (UC-24, N27).

SPEC §3.16 was written against this set after the fact and added two values
to it. Both earn their place by being separately *filterable*:

* ``retention_changed`` is technically a ``setting_updated``, but it is the
  one setting whose change destroys data — "who shortened retention, and
  when" must be one filter, not a JSONB dig through every settings change.
* ``command_issued`` is a person reaching into an employee's **personally
  owned** phone. It is the only action in the product that acts on somebody
  else's hardware, and this log is the only place that is visible.

Adding a value is a migration, which is the point: the list is closed so
that "everything that happened" is answerable from one column.
AuditAction.title: AuditAction

AuditResponse.description: One thing that happened. Immutable, by database trigger.

detail.description: Before/after values and counts. Never a password, a token or an enrolment code (N26). Open by nature — this is a server-side record, not a device payload, so §8's allow-list does not apply.

AuditResponse.title: AuditResponse

BlockBreakdownResponse.description:
The radar chart (BonviZvonki ``GET /analytics/blocks``).

A block the rubric does not name is **left out** rather than sent with a
null percentage: we do not know what to divide it by, and a bar with no
scale is worse than a missing one.
BlockBreakdownResponse.title: BlockBreakdownResponse

BlockScoreOut.description: One rubric block, averaged over the window.

block.description: The rubric's own key. An open vocabulary on purpose: scores are written under a pinned rubric_version, so a block a later rubric adds must still be readable. The panel renders an unknown key as the key.

max.description: From the rubric, never a second constant. The two were once typed separately, diverged 25 against 15, and the radar chart drew 106 % in front of a manager.

percent.description: score/max. The radar chart's axis, which is why it is bounded.

scored_calls.description: Calls this block's average is taken over.

BlockScoreOut.title: BlockScoreOut

force.description: Defaults to true, unlike the single-group send. The whole point of the button is 'send to everyone now'; silently sending nothing because of a ten-day window would be the broken behaviour.

BroadcastResponse.description:
What the broadcast did. The three numbers always account for every group.

``created + reused + len(skipped) == total_groups`` is an invariant, and a
test asserts it. "8 sent" on its own made an admin go and count rows on the
groups page to find out what happened to the rest.

delivered.description: How many were actually posted. **Zero in this deployment** — see `DispatchResponse.delivered`.

reused.description: Groups that already had an unsent survey queued.

BroadcastResponse.title: BroadcastResponse

BroadcastSkip.description: One group the broadcast passed over, and why.
BroadcastSkip.title: BroadcastSkip

BulkPatchRequest.description: The same change applied to many groups at once.
BulkPatchRequest.title: BulkPatchRequest

CallAnalysisResponse.description:
Everything the detail page needs, in one request (§6.2, §7.4).

``state``, ``transcript`` and ``score`` are **independently nullable**. A
call the pipeline has never touched answers 200 with all three null — not
404, because the page must be able to tell "not analysed" from "no such
call", and only one of those two is worth an error.

``enabled`` is repeated here rather than left to ``/analysis/status`` for
the same reason: deciding what to render must not cost two round trips to
learn a boolean.

enabled.description: `analysis.enabled`. False plus a null state means the page says 'o'chirilgan' and offers no button — pressing it would 409 (§7.4).

CallAnalysisResponse.title: CallAnalysisResponse

CallAudioSummary.description:
What the call list and the detail page need to know about the audio.

``capture_route`` is here and not folded into "audio: yes/no" because
``S1-RECORDING.md`` is explicit that ``app_voice_recognition`` and
``app_mic`` must stay distinguishable: the per-model capture rate is the M0
baseline, and UC-23's regression alert compares against it. Collapsing the
routes would make "which mechanism actually works on this handset" an
unanswerable question.

available.description: Playable now — stored and not yet expired.

capture_route.description: Which strategy produced it (S1, M0, UC-23).

capture_route_detail.description: The folder name only, never a path from the phone.

duration_mismatch.description: The file's length disagrees with the call log (UC-14).

url.description: Path to stream from, present only when the recording is available. A path and never a signed or public URL (N20): the endpoint is token-protected, and the panel reaches it through the Service Worker bridge because a plain <audio src> cannot send an Authorization header (T153, N43).

CallAudioSummary.title: CallAudioSummary

CallDirection.description:
Ours, not BonviZvonki's ``inbound``/``outbound``.

The export (SPEC §4.9) maps ours onto theirs in exactly one place, so the
two vocabularies never leak into each other.
CallDirection.title: CallDirection

CallDisposition.description:
UC-11's five classes are direction x disposition.

``missed`` and ``rejected`` are incoming-only, ``no_answer`` is
outgoing-only — enforced by a CHECK, so the invalid combinations are
unrepresentable rather than merely unused.
CallDisposition.title: CallDisposition

CallListResponse.description:
A cursor page of calls (SPEC §4.0).

``total`` is computed only when the caller asks: a COUNT(*) over a filtered
500k table is affordable once per filter change and not once per page.
CallListResponse.title: CallListResponse

CallResponse.description:
A call as the panel reads it.

Carries the display fields, not only ids. Making the browser look up an
agent's name per row is the N+1 problem relocated to the client, and the
``device_model`` filter would otherwise exist server-side for a column the
panel cannot show.

agent_name.description: Resolved server-side; the panel renders it.

device_model.description: 'Xiaomi Redmi Note 12'. The device_model filter needs it.

number_e164.description: The registered line the call happened on.

CallResponse.title: CallResponse

CallSentiment.description: The model's reading of how the conversation went.
CallSentiment.title: CallSentiment

CallStatsBucket.description:
One point on the x-axis: UC-11's five classes, counted.

Every bucket in the window is returned, including the empty ones. A chart
that receives only the days something happened draws a straight line
through a silent week, which is the one thing this chart exists to show.

date_to.description: Inclusive, and equal to date_from for a daily bucket. The last bucket is clipped to today, so a part-month is not drawn as a whole one.

total.description: Every call in the bucket, which is what the same filter returns from /calls — not necessarily the sum of the five classes.

CallStatsBucket.title: CallStatsBucket

CallStatsResponse.description: ``GET /api/v1/calls/stats`` — the call flow the dashboard draws.
CallStatsResponse.title: CallStatsResponse

CallType.description:
Internal vs external (UC-25). ``unknown`` is the mandatory default.

An empty line directory yields ``unknown``, never ``external``:
BonviZvonki defaulted to external and 82 of 98 calls were mislabelled.
CallType.title: CallType

CallTypeCountsOut.description:
Calls by type, over the window. **Every key is always present.**

A fixed object rather than a map, so a type with nothing in it is a visible
zero instead of an absent key the panel defaults for itself — which is how
the two lists drift apart. The fields are pinned against ``CallType`` by a
test.

**Deliberately not narrowed to scored calls.** This is the breakdown that
explains the headline: the ``calls`` metric counts *scored* conversations,
and without this row a manager who sees "6" in a month of 22,000 calls
concludes the system lost the rest. Measured in BonviZvonki: 72 against
22,026 for the same period.
CallTypeCountsOut.title: CallTypeCountsOut

Capability.description:
One row per installation per capability (UC-03, §7.8).

Every one of these is verified by exercising it, never by reading a
permission flag — that is what makes ``granted_not_working`` expressible.
Capability.title: Capability

CapabilityState.description: ``granted_not_working`` is the OEM-permission-manager case UC-03 names.
CapabilityState.title: CapabilityState

CapabilityStateResponse.description:
One capability's current state, as the panel's matrix renders it.

A **required** capability the phone has never reported appears here as
``unknown`` with null timestamps, rather than being absent. Absence made
the page show every row green while ``capturing`` was false, with nothing
on screen saying which capability was missing — and a phone stuck part-way
through E2 is exactly that shape.

changed_at.description: Null until there is a state to have changed from.

checked_at.description: Null when this capability has never been checked.

CapabilityStateResponse.title: CapabilityStateResponse

CaptureRoute.description:
Which mechanism produced the recording (S1, the M0 baseline).

``NONE`` may only appear with ``has_audio = false``.
CaptureRoute.title: CaptureRoute

new_password.description: Minimum 10 characters and no other composition rule (SPEC §4.7): a rule people cannot follow is a rule they write on a sticky note.

ClientAgentRow.description: An employee who spoke to this customer.
ClientAgentRow.title: ClientAgentRow

received_at.description: Shown beside `started_at` because the two differ whenever a phone was off or a recovery sweep found an old call (SPEC §3.12).

ClientCallsResponse.description: One keyset page of this customer's conversations, newest first.
ClientCallsResponse.title: ClientCallsResponse

ClientDetailResponse.description: The card: the same aggregate as the list row, plus who spoke to them.

agents.description: Employees who spoke to this customer, most first.

scope.description: The cut the customer was actually FOUND in. It can differ from the one asked for: a card link with no `scope` on it would otherwise never open an internal number. The panel echoes it so the two lists below the card are asked with the same cut.

ClientDetailResponse.title: ClientDetailResponse

ClientKind.description:
Sales control is split into **two separate sections**.

⚠️ WHY THEY CANNOT BE MIXED. A walk-in buyer is never written into the
catalogue by name and number — they pass under one of a few shared codes
(``sales.walk_in_codes``). For a sale under such a code the question "was
this customer spoken to first?" is meaningless: one code, a hundred people.
They used to sit in the same list as regular customers and were counted as
``not_checkable``, which wrote "could not be checked" into an employee's
column — when what it actually described was the KIND OF WORK, not the
quality of our data.

Measured (24.08.2026): 718 sales and $531,432 under ``К00001`` alone — a
sizeable share of what looked like the regular-customer list.

· :attr:`REGULAR` — regular customers. Shared codes are EXCLUDED.
· :attr:`WALK_IN` — shared codes only. The rules do not apply; the measure
  is different — is any single ticket over the limit.
ClientKind.title: ClientKind

ClientPageResponse.description: One keyset page of the directory.

next_cursor.description: Opaque. Pass it back as `cursor`; null means this is the last page.

total.description: How many customers the filter matches. Only the FIRST page asks for it (`with_total`), so every later page answers null — a count over a grouped aggregate is affordable once per filter change and not once per page.

ClientPageResponse.title: ClientPageResponse

ClientRowOut.description: One customer in the directory — one phone number and its history.

agent_count.description: How many employees have spoken to them.

code.description: The customer code read out of the contact name. Null — the dictionary holds no code for this number.

first_call_at.description: Null — there was no contact inside the chosen period. That is not the same as an unknown customer: the card still opens and shows zeros.

main_agent_name.description: Whoever spoke to them most. The list shows this one and `+N`.

missed.description: Incoming and unanswered — the company's responsibility. The same definition the activity report uses: `rejected` counts here with `missed`, because the phone rang and there was no conversation.

missed_rate.description: Missed as a percent of incoming. Null when there were none.

name.description: The uploaded contact list first, the handset's own resolution as the fallback. Null — nobody has ever named this number.

phone_key.description: The last-9 matching key (`calls.remote_number_key`, N37). The identifier for both the list and the card, and the same value `MissedClientRow.phone_key` carries.

scored.description: How many conversations were scored — what the average is over.

ClientRowOut.title: ClientRowOut

ClientScope.description:
Who is in the list.

``CLIENTS`` is the default: everything except internal conversations. It is
deliberately NOT a strict "external only" filter — unclassified rows
(``call_type = 'unknown'``) can exist and being unclassified does not mean
"not a customer", it means not yet decided. Hiding them quietly would make
the list incomplete.

⚠️ The source has to write this as ``call_type IS NULL OR call_type <>
'internal'`` and carries a comment about why: in SQL ``NULL <> 'internal'``
is NULL, so unclassified rows vanish silently. BonviCall's ``call_type`` is
a NOT NULL enum defaulting to ``unknown`` (UC-25 — an empty line directory
yields ``unknown``, never ``external``), so the plain inequality is correct
here and the NULL guard is dropped rather than translated.
ClientScope.title: ClientScope

ClientSort.description: What the directory is ordered by.
ClientSort.title: ClientSort

CommandFailureReason.description: Why a command did not happen. UC-16 requires the panel to say which.
CommandFailureReason.title: CommandFailureReason

CommandKind.description: Server-to-device commands. No ``send_sms`` — SMS is out of scope.
CommandKind.title: CommandKind

latency_ms.description: acked_at - created_at, stored so UC-16's five-second bar is **measured** rather than assumed. R3 flags that bar as possibly unachievable on doze-restricted OEMs; this column is what turns that into a conversation with evidence.

ComplianceItem.description:
One sale: the SAP fact, the verdict, and THE EVIDENCE.

The evidence fields (`last_call_at` … `calls_total`) are not optional
decoration. The manager re-derives the number by hand, so every suspicious
row has to carry "when was the last conversation, with whom, how many days
before" beside it. Without that the list is not believed.

agent_id.description: Whoever SPOKE to the customer, else whoever holds the branch. Null when neither is known — that sale belongs to nobody yet.

amount_usd.description: The same amount in dollars, straight from SAP. Stored as `numeric`; every comparison against a threshold happens in SQL, so no client ever has to compare money as a float.

broken_rules.description: Always in this order (R1, R2, R3) so badges do not move about.

calls_between.description: Conversations between the previous sale and this one (R2).

calls_total.description: Conversations in the WHOLE history, the period included and not bounded by it — R3 is the harshest signal and is stated in its most cautious form.

days_before.description: Days before the sale. `0` — the same day.

doc_number.description: SAP's `Номер документа` — the piece of paper the manager searches for. NOT interchangeable with `external_id`.

last_call_at.description: The nearest conversation before the sale (or on its own day). NOT bounded by the window: a conversation nine days ago is still shown, because that number is what explains the rule.

last_call_id.description: The call row itself, so the panel can open the recording. BonviZvonki shows a date and a name with nothing behind them.

occurred_on.description: A DATE with no time — SAP gives no clock for a sale.

over_limit.description: A walk-in sale over the single-ticket limit. ALWAYS false in the regular-customer section: a large sale to a regular customer is a normal event.

partner_code.description: The customer. A customer IS the code.

partner_excluded.description: The customer is out of sales control. Does not affect the verdict — it is for the BUTTON: without it the card would open saying 'Exclude' even for a customer already excluded, and there would be no way back from the screen.

phone.description: As SAP wrote it — for display, never for matching.

phone_key.description: The last-9 key the match was made on (N37).

previous_sale_on.description: This customer's previous sale. Null — a FIRST sale, so R2 is silent.

renders a binding renders which of these it rests on.
